claims.statement: The governing HO-3 edition is selected by policy-written date: 2011-05 remains in force for policies written under it regardless of when a loss is reported, while 2018-09 applies to policies written on or after 2018-09-01.

Both supplied HO-3 editions exclude water or waterborne material backing up through sewers or drains and sump-related overflow or discharge under A.3 unless HO 04 90 is attached; 2018-09 additionally states the exception is subject to the endorsement sublimit and its A.3 exclusion includes mechanical-breakdown-caused backup or overflow.

When HO 04 90 (2010-10) is attached, W.1 writes back the selected HO-3 A.3 exclusion only for direct physical loss to Coverage A, B, or C property from the described sewer/drain backup or sump-related overflow or discharge, including an event resulting from mechanical breakdown.

HO 04 90 W.4 separately preserves the selected HO-3 A.1 exclusion for flood, surface water, waves, tidal water, storm surge, and overflow of a body of water, whether or not driven by wind; the W.1 A.3 write-back is not flood coverage.

HO 04 90 W.4 separately preserves the selected HO-3 A.2 exclusion for water below the surface of the ground, including the stated pressure, seepage, or leakage through structures; the W.1 A.3 write-back does not turn an A.2 source into a covered sump event.
Only HO-3 2018-09 adds A.4, under which A.1 through A.3 apply regardless of any other cause or event contributing concurrently or in any sequence to the loss.

For HO-3 2018-09, Coverage A/B are insured for direct physical loss except as excluded, whereas Coverage C is limited to named perils including accidental discharge or overflow of water or steam from within plumbing, heating, or air-conditioning systems.

HO-3 2018-09 C.3 excludes continuous or repeated water or steam seepage or leakage over weeks, months, or years from the listed internal systems or household appliances, but preserves loss that is sudden and accidental; Definition 5 requires abrupt, unintended onset and rejects a gradually developing or known-unremedied condition regardless of when effects become apparent.

Attached HO 04 90 has a $5,000 maximum for all endorsement loss in one policy period unless its Declarations show a higher limit, and that sublimit is part of—not additional to—the applicable Coverage A, B, and C limits.

For each covered HO 04 90 loss, W.3 modifies the selected base Section I deductible rather than writing back coverage: it applies a separate $500 deductible and makes the Section I Declarations deductible inapplicable to that loss.

Where Coverage C loss is covered under HO 04 90, W.6 modifies the base C.2 settlement result rather than writing back coverage: it requires actual cash value despite a replacement-cost personal-property endorsement unless the endorsement Declarations state otherwise; W.6 leaves Coverage A/B loss on the attached policy's settlement basis.

HO 04 90 W.5 bars endorsement coverage where the backup, overflow, or discharge resulted from a known pre-loss failure by an insured to maintain the serving sewer line, drain, sump, or pump that a reasonable person would have remedied.
HO 04 90 leaves all other policy provisions applicable, so its A.3 write-back does not bypass other property, exclusion, condition, or declaration controls.

For the supplied 2018-09 form, HO 04 81 M.1 writes back HO-3 C.2 only for qualifying fungi, wet/dry rot, or bacteria resulting from a Section I insured peril during the policy period; M.2 separately preserves the A.1 flood/surface-water, A.2 subsurface-water, and C.3 continuous-or-repeated-leakage barriers, while identifying backup covered by an attached water-backup endorsement as a covered-moisture example.

Internal water-loss guidance requires source-first documentation and directs technical referral for uncertain or competing sources, foundation losses, public-adjuster/counsel involvement, losses above $25,000, or a duration-based denial; it directs a reservation of rights before investigating when duration or the HO 04 90 maintenance condition may control, and expressly says it is not policy language to quote to an insured or claimant.

Florida and Texas underwriting guidance treats HO 04 90 as optional coverage written by attachment, imposes state-specific water-backup limit and below-grade battery-backed-sump controls, and instructs that it must not be represented as flood coverage; these internal guides are not policy contracts.

HO-3 2018-09 P.2 names accidental discharge or overflow from within plumbing, heating, or air-conditioning systems as a Coverage C peril but does not name household appliances in that peril; the supplied 2011-05 text contains no separately numbered P.1/P.2 perils-insured-against section, so the 2018 gate should not be imported into a 2011-05 analysis.

HO 04 90 W.5 is a distinct pre-loss condition from base C.1 neglect: it bars endorsement loss only where a known failure to maintain the serving sewer line, drain, sump, or pump caused the event and a reasonable person would have remedied it, while C.1 addresses reasonable preservation at and after a loss.

HO 04 90 2010-10 remains in force for policies written under that edition regardless of loss-report date, while HO 04 90 2027-01 applies to policies written on or after 2027-01-01; the issued endorsement edition therefore controls its terms.

When attached, HO 04 90 2027-01 W.1 provides the same limited direct-physical-loss route as 2010-10 for Coverage A, B, and C property damaged by the described sewer/drain backup or sump-related overflow/discharge, whether or not mechanical breakdown caused it.

For a covered HO 04 90 2027-01 loss, W.2 sets a $10,000 maximum for all endorsement loss in one policy period unless the Declarations show a higher limit, W.3 substitutes a separate $1,000 deductible for the Section I deductible, and W.7 keeps A/B on the attached-policy settlement basis while requiring Coverage C actual cash value unless the endorsement Declarations state otherwise.

HO 04 90 2027-01 W.6 makes endorsement coverage for premises with a finished area below grade conditional on an installed and operable backwater valve or equivalent backflow-prevention device on the serving sewer line at the time of loss; that requirement is absent from HO 04 90 2010-10.
Both HO 04 90 editions preserve the selected HO-3 A.1 flood/surface-water and A.2 subsurface-water exclusions in W.4, so their A.3 write-back is not flood or subsurface-water coverage.
